description: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational application developed by team MarsCode that allows children to experience the role of real astronauts and space engineers. Moving away from meaningless entertainment, we create an environment where every gaming mechanic is grounded in real physical laws, astronomy, and the logic of actual space flights.
summary: Solix brings deep-space exploration to life for kids ages 7–12 through an interactive mission simulator. Young astronauts take command of a Martian outpost, making high-stakes decisions under real pressure: should limited power go to life support or radiation shielding during an incoming solar flare? Guided by an assistant that translates complex space terminology on the fly, players learn how every action shapes their mission’s success. Blending real NASA open data with immersive audio and gameplay, Solix transforms space science from a textbook lesson into an unforgettable adventure.
details:
What does it do?
Solix is an interactive, gamified mission trainer designed to take young explorers (ages 7–12) on a complete journey to Mars. The gameplay flows through intuitive stages:
Main Menu: an engaging starting hub that welcomes young astronauts.
Crew Selection: players assemble their own mission crew, making critical introductory choices.
Flight to Mars: a simulated space transit phase introducing space travel dynamics.
The Martian Outpost Expedition: the core experience where players manage a 7-day surface mission. Throughout the expedition, children can read or listen to audio briefings, track daily tasks, and make real survival trade-offs (such as balancing water vs. food, managing power supplies, and protecting the base against solar radiation and dust storms). An assistant helps simplify complex space terminology on the fly.


What benefits does it have?
While most space educational tools either oversimplify concepts into abstract facts or overwhelm kids with technical jargon, Solix focuses on extreme simplification and tangibility. We don't try to build an overly complex simulation; instead, we make real engineering constraints intuitive and fun. The impact is simple: children move beyond passive screen time to understand how a real space mission works, how every decision has a consequence, and what it takes to survive on another planet.


What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
Core Engine: Unity (C#) for real-time rendering, scene management, and resource loop mechanics.
3D Assets & UI/UX: Blender for 3D modeling (outpost modules, rovers, Martian terrain) and Figma for kid-friendly UI/UX design.
Data Integration: Python scripts to pre-process open APIs from NASA and partner agencies into a unified mars_outpost_master.json dataset, leveraging:
NASA DONKI: Real space weather events (solar flares like M7.6 and X9.0) driving mission alerts.
NASA RadLab & OSDR: Real radiation metrics (orbit and surface dosimeters) and biological research guiding module reinforcement mechanics.
NASA Mars Trek & CSA (Space Food Toolkit): Jezero Crater landing coordinates and closed-loop life support models.


How is your project creative?
Solix creatively bridges the gap between hard NASA open data and childhood imagination. By turning complex scientific datasets (like space weather catalogs and radiation dosimeters) into playful, audio-supported narrative choices and visual mechanics, we transform raw data into an accessible adventure.
